architectural_implications.after: A 3:1 interleaving of Kimi Delta Attention (chunkwise, recurrent-state) with full attention layers.
architectural_implications.before: Uniform full self-attention in every layer, with a single KV-cache growth model and quadratic long-context cost.
architectural_implications.consequence: Serving runtimes must account for mixed layer types: memory budgeting, chunk boundaries, matrix-inversion/state-update kernels, and batching/parallelism strategies differ per layer class, and long-context TPOT becomes a configurable rather than fixed property.
architectural_implications.observation: Attention layer composition is no longer homogeneous across the stack.

architectural_implications.after: An orchestrator that spawns specialist sub-agents in parallel, optimized with instantiation, finish, and outcome rewards.
architectural_implications.before: A single agent with a long context and hand-written decomposition logic.
architectural_implications.consequence: Task decomposition becomes a learned policy with its own failure modes (serial collapse, spurious parallelism), so harnesses need per-agent lifecycle telemetry, spawn/terminate accounting, and cost attribution to detect useless parallelism.
architectural_implications.observation: Multi-agent swarms are trained end-to-end with reward shaping over orchestration behavior, not assembled from a static planner.

architectural_implications.after: Attention residuals / block attention residuals, motivated as an LSTM residual rotated into attention space.
architectural_implications.before: Standard identity residual (x + f(x)) repeated uniformly across layers.
architectural_implications.consequence: Layer-level memory and gradient-flow properties change, so architecture search and ablation budgets shift from layer count/width toward residual topology.
architectural_implications.observation: The residual stream itself becomes a design surface.

architectural_implications.after: Early fusion: native joint vision-text pretraining.
architectural_implications.before: Late fusion: adapters or projection heads attached to a text-pretrained backbone.
architectural_implications.consequence: Data pipeline, tokenizer, sequence packing, and training-time modality mixing become coupled concerns; vision RL can feed back into text quality, so modality experiments stop being isolated feature work.
architectural_implications.observation: Multimodal integration moves from the post-training/integration layer into pretraining.

article_ideas.angle: Translate the reward-shaping result into concrete harness instrumentation requirements: spawn/terminate accounting, marginal-contribution logging, and cost-per-quality dashboards.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building multi-agent orchestrators and agent harnesses
article_ideas.based_on: spurious parallelism (spawning agents that contribute nothing)
article_ideas.thesis: Once task decomposition is trained with spawn and terminate rewards, the decomposition policy acquires its own failure modes — serial collapse and spurious parallelism — so agent harnesses need per-agent lifecycle telemetry and cost attribution at the same priority as the final task score; teams that measure only task success will pay for parallelism they never received.
article_ideas.title: Your Orchestrator Is a Learned Policy, Not a Planner

article_ideas.angle: Reframe efficiency research as a multiplier on a capped resource and demand matched-baseline ablations before treating any headline number as portable.
article_ideas.audience: Pretraining leads and research engineering managers allocating data vs compute budget
article_ideas.thesis: If halving tokens-per-unit-intelligence is equivalent to doubling the usable high-quality corpus, then optimizer and architecture work should be budgeted against data-acquisition economics — and headline efficiency multipliers must ship with ablations separating the optimizer from its weight-decay and update-normalization components.
article_ideas.title: Token Efficiency Is a Data-Acquisition Strategy, Not an Optimizer Tuning Detail

article_ideas.angle: Walk through which runtime assumptions (single KV-growth model, homogeneous kernels, fixed TPOT profile) stop holding and what must replace them.
article_ideas.based_on: 3:1 ratio of linear to full attention layers
article_ideas.thesis: A mixture of linear-to-full attention layers turns time-per-output-token and memory overhead into configurable properties, which means schedulers, paging, batching, and chunk-boundary kernels must be re-derived per layer class instead of inherited from a uniform-transformer runtime.
article_ideas.title: Hybrid 3:1 Attention Breaks Your Serving Stack's Assumptions

article_ideas.angle: Argue the residual path is an under-explored design surface and specify the ablation matrix needed to promote it from curiosity to default.
article_ideas.based_on: Attention Residuals improve token efficiency by 24%
article_ideas.thesis: If reshaping residuals buys double-digit token efficiency, residual topology deserves the ablation budget currently spent on layer count and width — but AttnRes must first be validated on hybrid recurrent stacks, since a gain proven only on full-attention blocks is not yet a general-purpose gain.
article_ideas.title: The Residual Stream Is Not Settled Infrastructure

connections.connects_to: stable training of very large transformers
connections.relationship: QK-Clip is the stabilization mechanism that makes the token-efficiency gain from Muon usable at 1T scale, so efficiency and stability are coupled rather than independent.

connections.connects_to: Attention Residuals (LSTM residual rotated into attention space)
connections.relationship: Both are recurrence-flavored ideas injected into the transformer: one replaces full attention with a gated recurrent memory, the other generalizes residual connections along the same recurrence/attention duality.
Orchestration policy quality becomes an RL optimization problem with shaped rewards, meaning agent harness design now depends on reward engineering and failure-mode monitoring.
Optimizer/architecture efficiency is reframed as an equivalent expansion of the finite high-quality data budget, linking pretraining research directly to data acquisition economics.

connections.connects_to: cross-modal transfer from vision RL to text
connections.relationship: Joint pretraining is the enabling condition that lets multimodal RL feed back into text capability rather than only adding vision as a downstream feature.

evidence_quotes.text: Reinforcement learning for agent swarms requires instantiation, finish, and outcome rewards to prevent serial collapse and spurious parallelism.
Agent swarms save significant execution time on complex tasks compared to single agents.

core_insights.generalization: Any orchestrator/worker architecture (including non-RL planners) needs explicit incentives or heuristics for spawn justification and termination, otherwise fan-out cost is paid without parallelism benefit.
core_insights.insight: Reward shaping for orchestrator-driven agent swarms requires at least three distinct reward signals — instantiation, finish, and outcome — specifically to prevent two degenerate behaviors: serial collapse (the orchestrator does everything itself) and spurious parallelism (spawning agents that contribute nothing).
core_insights.why_it_matters: Multi-agent speedups are not automatic; without explicit rewards for when to spawn and when to terminate sub-agents, the orchestrator degenerates into either a single serial agent or wasteful fan-out. This tells builders that the decomposition policy itself is a learned, reward-shaped artifact rather than a static planner rule, and that harnesses need per-behavior reward instrumentation, not just a final task-success signal.

evidence_quotes.text: combining Delta Attention with a 3:1 ratio of linear to full attention layers to achieve linear scaling and superior long-context performance
Kimi Linear architecture achieves better performance than full attention baselines while cutting memory overhead.
Drastically reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) at long context lengths.

core_insights.generalization: Hybrid layer-ratio architectures are a tunable knob between expressivity and memory/compute cost, applicable wherever a recurrent or compressed-state layer can substitute for some full-attention layers.
core_insights.insight: Kimi Linear uses a hybrid stack with a 3:1 ratio of Kimi Delta Attention (linear) layers to full attention layers, with a chunkwise formulation, and reportedly beats full-attention baselines while cutting memory overhead.
core_insights.why_it_matters: The design claim is that you do not need pure linear attention or pure full attention: a fixed ratio mixture preserves expressivity while getting linear-scaling economics. For serving stacks this shifts the KV-cache/memory budget and the time-per-output-token profile at long context, so the scheduler, paging, and batching assumptions of a standard transformer runtime no longer hold unchanged.

evidence_quotes.text: Scaling a 1-trillion parameter model with Muon and encountering max logit explosions solved by QK-Clip.
Training instability during large-scale Muon training can be resolved using QK-Clip.

core_insights.generalization: Aggressive optimizers can be stabilized by constraining the specific parameter subspace that produces the blowup, instead of globally reducing step size and giving back the efficiency gain.
core_insights.insight: Scaling the Muon optimizer to a 1-trillion-parameter model caused max logits to explode; QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to restore stability, enabling ~2x token efficiency over AdamW without divergence.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Second-order/orthogonalized optimizers buy token efficiency but introduce a specific, diagnosable failure mode (attention logit blowup) that must be handled architecturally rather than by lowering learning rate. This gives practitioners a concrete instability signature to watch (max logits) and a targeted intervention (clipping Q/K projections) rather than a generic 'training is unstable' heuristic.

evidence_quotes.text: Attention Residuals improve token efficiency by 24% and reduce training loss.
introduces Attention Residuals (AttnRes) as a rotation of LSTM residuals into attention space

core_insights.generalization: Cross-pollinating recurrence structure into attention topology (and vice versa) is a productive source of architectural gain, and residual-path redesign is measurable in token efficiency, not just in loss curves.
core_insights.insight: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) are framed as an LSTM residual rotated into attention space and applied as block attention residuals; they are reported to improve token efficiency by 24% and reduce training loss.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes residual connections as a form of recurrence that can be rotated/generalized rather than a fixed identity skip. If a residual-connection variant alone yields double-digit token efficiency gains, the residual stream is an under-explored design surface, not settled infrastructure — worth prototyping before adding more data or parameters.

evidence_quotes.text: Early fusion vision-text joint pretraining yields better results than late fusion.
Vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance (cross-modal transfer).
first open model with native joint vision-text pretraining

core_insights.generalization: Modality fusion at pretraining time can act as a regularizer/capability multiplier for the primary modality, so modality investment should be budgeted as core training rather than as a downstream feature.
core_insights.insight: Early-fusion (native joint) vision-text pretraining outperforms late fusion, and vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance — i.e., cross-modal transfer flows from vision training into text capability.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This challenges the common practice of bolting a vision encoder onto a frozen or lightly tuned text model with adapters. It implies multimodal capability is a pretraining-pipeline decision, not a post-hoc integration layer, and that multimodal RL is not merely additive to text quality.

evidence_quotes.text: Token efficiency improves the upper bound of model intelligence, acting like a data multiplier.
Scaling must happen across multiple dimensions: token efficiency, context length, and agent swarms.

core_insights.generalization: When a resource is capped (data, budget, latency), efficiency gains in that resource should be evaluated as multipliers on the capped quantity, not as incremental speedups.
core_insights.insight: Kimi frames scaling as three parallel dimensions — token efficiency, context length, and agent swarms — rather than a single axis of parameters or FLOPs, with token efficiency treated as a data multiplier that raises the ceiling of achievable intelligence under a fixed high-quality data budget.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes the binding constraint as data quality/quantity rather than compute, which changes investment priority: optimizer and architecture work that halves tokens-per-unit-intelligence is equivalent to doubling the usable corpus, and is therefore cheaper than acquiring new data. It also gives a portfolio framing for roadmap decisions across training, serving, and agent layers.

evidence_quotes.text: Reinforcement learning for agent swarms requires instantiation, finish, and outcome rewards to prevent serial collapse and spurious parallelism.
Execution time vs task complexity graphs showing up to 4.5x speedups.

deep_dives.research_question: Do the instantiation/finish/outcome reward signals produce spawn-efficient orchestration on task families other than the reported parallel-research workloads, or do they overfit and invite reward hacking?
deep_dives.topic: Cross-domain transfer and reward hacking of the three swarm reward signals
deep_dives.why: Spawn/terminate behavior is a learned policy with its own degenerate regimes; if the reward mix only works on one task family, teams copying the recipe will pay fan-out cost without parallelism benefit, and their task-success metric will not reveal it.

evidence_quotes.text: Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW.
Token efficiency improves the upper bound of model intelligence, acting like a data multiplier.

deep_dives.research_question: How much of the ~2x token efficiency over AdamW comes from Muon's orthogonalized updates versus weight decay and the RMS-update scheme, and does the ranking survive changes in scale and data distribution?
deep_dives.topic: Attribution of Muon's claimed ~2x token efficiency
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW
deep_dives.why: If most of the gain comes from regularization rather than the optimizer, teams can capture it on a standard optimizer without inheriting the max-logit stability tooling; if not, the efficiency claim justifies the full MuonClip stack and its operational cost.

evidence_quotes.text: Scaling a 1-trillion parameter model with Muon and encountering max logit explosions solved by QK-Clip.
Training instability during large-scale Muon training can be resolved using QK-Clip.

deep_dives.research_question: What subspace does QK-Clip constrain, and does clipping query/key projections degrade attention sharpness, long-context retrieval, or interact with hybrid linear-attention layers?
deep_dives.topic: QK-Clip mechanism, clip-threshold sensitivity, and its cost to attention expressivity
deep_dives.trigger_insight: QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to restore stability
deep_dives.why: QK-Clip is what makes the Muon token-efficiency gain usable at trillion-parameter scale; if it silently refunds that gain as reduced long-context retrieval quality, the two headline results cannot be treated as independent wins.

evidence_quotes.text: Attention Residuals improve token efficiency by 24% and reduce training loss.
Kimi Linear architecture achieves better performance than full attention baselines while cutting memory overhead.

deep_dives.research_question: Do AttnRes's 24% token-efficiency gains persist when residual topology is placed over recurrent-state (KDA) layers, or do the gains assume homogeneous full-attention blocks?
deep_dives.topic: Attention Residuals composed with hybrid 3:1 KDA/full-attention stacks
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) are framed as an LSTM residual rotated into attention space
deep_dives.why: Both AttnRes and Kimi Linear are recurrence-flavored modifications to the same stack; if they are reported separately with no interaction ablation, an architecture team cannot know whether to adopt one, both, or neither.

evidence_quotes.text: Early fusion vision-text joint pretraining yields better results than late fusion.
Vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance (cross-modal transfer).

deep_dives.research_question: Does vision RL on a shared backbone improve text benchmarks beyond an equal-compute text-only RL control, or is the gain simply additional RL compute applied to the same parameters?
deep_dives.topic: Isolating cross-modal transfer from vision RL into text capability
deep_dives.trigger_insight: vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance
deep_dives.why: If the transfer is real it justifies budgeting modality work as core training rather than as a downstream feature; if it is a compute artifact, teams that add vision RL expecting text gains will misallocate training budget.

project_ideas.name: Spawn Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an orchestrator/worker harness so every spawn, termination, sub-agent token cost, and each sub-agent's marginal effect on the outcome is logged; replay one task suite under outcome-only reward versus instantiation+finish+outcome reward.

project_ideas.based_on: QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to restore stability
project_ideas.hypothesis: Max-logit trajectory is a measurable early-warning signal of large-scale optimizer divergence, and constraining query/key projections restores stability across seeds without degrading long-context retrieval beyond a bounded clip-threshold window.
project_ideas.measurement: Steps-to-divergence and max-logit slope per configuration; retrieval and loss deltas as a function of clip threshold and random seed.
project_ideas.name: Logit Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument per-step max logits during Muon-style training runs at multiple scales, sweep Q/K clip thresholds, and evaluate long-context retrieval and downstream loss at each threshold.

project_ideas.based_on: Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW
project_ideas.hypothesis: A measurable share of the reported ~2x token efficiency over AdamW is attributable to weight decay and RMS update normalization rather than to orthogonalized updates, distinguishable as tokens-to-target-loss at matched settings.
project_ideas.measurement: tokens-to-target-loss ratio per arm per scale, divergence rate per arm, and the portion of the reported multiplier retained once regularization is matched.
project_ideas.name: Efficiency Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run controlled ablations at several model scales comparing AdamW with matched weight decay and RMS normalization against Muon, with tokens-to-target-loss as the dependent variable.

project_ideas.based_on: Drastically reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) at long context lengths.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A runtime that models a 3:1 linear-to-full attention stack as two layer classes with distinct memory and state-update behavior predicts long-context time-per-output-token and peak memory within a small error margin, where a uniform-transformer model does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted versus observed TPOT and peak memory at long context, and the deviation of the uniform-transformer baseline's predictions from the same measurements.
project_ideas.name: Hybrid-KV Planner
project_ideas.poc: Build a scheduler/paging simulator with separate KV-cache growth for full-attention layers and fixed-size recurrent state for linear layers, then validate predictions against measured TPOT and memory across context lengths.

source.title: How We Scaled Kimi K2.5 | Zhilin Yang's full GTC 2026 Keynote

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Zhilin Yang
  • Channel: Kimi AI
  • Main topic: Scaling strategies for open-source AI models, focusing on Kimi K2.5, MuonClip optimizer, Kimi Linear attention, attention residuals, and agent swarms.
  • Purpose: To explain the architectural innovations and scaling laws employed by Moonshot AI in developing Kimi K2.5 and its associated open-source techniques. Zhilin Yang, Founder and CEO of Kimi (Moonshot AI), presents the scaling strategies behind Kimi K2.5 at NVIDIA GTC 2026. The talk covers three key scaling dimensions: token efficiency via MuonClip optimizer, long context via Kimi Linear attention, and agent swarms via multi-agent reinforcement learning. Additionally, it highlights Kimi K2.5 as the first open model with native joint vision-text pretraining, achieving superior performance across modalities.

Topic Map

Introduction to Kimi's Scaling Strategy

  • Explanation: Introduction of open models, democratizing intelligence, and the three primary scaling dimensions: token efficiency, long context, and agent swarms.
  • Key claims:
    • Open models are closing the gap with proprietary models.
    • Scaling is the primary driver of major AI developments.
    • Scaling must happen across multiple dimensions: token efficiency, context length, and agent swarms.
  • Examples:
    • Deploying open models on local servers or the cloud with full weight access.
  • Terminology:
    • open models
    • scaling law
    • token efficiency
    • long context
    • agent swarms
  • Why it matters: Establishes the foundational philosophy of making frontier intelligence accessible to developers worldwide.

Token Efficiency: MuonClip Optimizer

  • Explanation: Discusses scaling token efficiency using the Muon optimizer combined with weight decay and QK-Clip to achieve ~2x token efficiency over AdamW without training divergence.
  • Key claims:
    • Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW.
    • Training instability during large-scale Muon training can be resolved using QK-Clip.
    • Token efficiency improves the upper bound of model intelligence, acting like a data multiplier.
  • Examples:
    • Scaling a 1-trillion parameter model with Muon and encountering max logit explosions solved by QK-Clip.
  • Terminology:
    • Muon optimizer
    • MuonClip
    • weight decay
    • RMS updates
    • QK-Clip
    • max logits
  • Why it matters: Overcomes data wall limitations by maximizing intelligence per training token.

Long Context: Kimi Linear Attention (KDA)

  • Explanation: Introduces Kimi Linear Attention (KDA) and Kimi Linear Architecture, combining Delta Attention with a 3:1 ratio of linear to full attention layers to achieve linear scaling and superior long-context performance.
  • Key claims:
    • Transformers outperform LSTMs asymptotically due to long-context utilization across the whole context.
    • Kimi Delta Attention improves recurrent memory management and hardware efficiency.
    • Kimi Linear architecture achieves better performance than full attention baselines while cutting memory overhead.
  • Examples:
    • Comparing transformer and LSTM token-index scaling curves and benchmarking Kimi Linear on MMLU and RULER.
  • Terminology:
    • Kimi Delta Attention (KDA)
    • Gated Delta Rule (GDR)
    • Kimi Linear
    • chunkwise formulation
    • matrix inversion
  • Why it matters: Enables efficient processing of million-token context lengths without quadratic compute penalties.

Agent Swarms and Reinforcement Learning

  • Explanation: Explains the multi-agent swarm paradigm where an orchestrator agent delegates complex tasks to specialized sub-agents working in parallel, guided by specific reinforcement learning reward functions.
  • Key claims:
    • Agent swarms scale task complexity beyond single-agent capabilities.
    • Reinforcement learning for agent swarms requires instantiation, finish, and outcome rewards to prevent serial collapse and spurious parallelism.
    • Agent swarms save significant execution time on complex tasks compared to single agents.
  • Examples:
    • Writing a 100-page literature review by spawning specialized researchers and fact-checkers in parallel.
  • Terminology:
    • agent swarms
    • orchestrator
    • sub-agents
    • instantiation reward
    • finish reward
    • outcome reward
  • Why it matters: Solves complex, multi-step workflows by orchestrating collaborative intelligence.

Vision-Text Joint Pretraining & Attention Residuals

  • Explanation: Presents Kimi K2.5 as the first open model with native joint vision-text pretraining (early fusion) and introduces Attention Residuals (AttnRes) as a rotation of LSTM residuals into attention space.
  • Key claims:
    • Early fusion vision-text joint pretraining yields better results than late fusion.
    • Vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance (cross-modal transfer).
    • Attention Residuals improve token efficiency by 24% and reduce training loss.
  • Examples:
    • Training Kimi K2.5 on NVIDIA H800 clusters and demonstrating code, vision, and text capabilities.
  • Terminology:
    • early fusion
    • vision-text joint pretraining
    • Attention Residuals (AttnRes)
    • block attention residual
  • Why it matters: Unifies vision and text natively while introducing breakthrough architectural components.

Key Points

MuonClip doubles token efficiency over AdamW

  • Explanation: By applying the second-order Muon optimizer with weight decay and consistent RMS updates, model training achieves equivalent intelligence with half the tokens.
  • Evidence: Scaling law graphs showing ~2x token efficiency vs AdamW.
  • Practical implication: Reduces training compute requirements and effectively expands limited high-quality data budgets.

QK-Clip stabilizes large-scale Muon training

  • Explanation: Scaling Muon to 1-trillion parameter models causes max logits to explode; QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to prevent divergence.
  • Evidence: Validation loss and max logits training curves before and after QK-Clip.
  • Practical implication: Allows stable training of large transformer models with advanced second-order optimizers.

Kimi Linear Attention balances efficiency and expressivity

  • Explanation: Using a 3:1 ratio of linear attention (Kimi Delta Attention) to full attention layers with chunkwise formulation cuts memory overhead while outperforming full attention.
  • Evidence: Performance benchmarks on RULER and MMLU across 128k to 1M token lengths.
  • Practical implication: Drastically reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) at long context lengths.

Agent swarms accelerate complex task execution

  • Explanation: Orchestrator-driven agent swarms decompose complex tasks into parallel subtasks, using specialized RL reward functions to ensure successful task completion.
  • Evidence: Execution time vs task complexity graphs showing up to 4.5x speedups.
  • Practical implication: Enables automated execution of complex workflows like software engineering and comprehensive research.

Attention Residuals generalize residual connections

  • Explanation: Treating attention as an LSTM residual rotated by 90 degrees and applying attention residuals across layers improves pretraining token efficiency by 24%.
  • Evidence: Scaling law and benchmark comparison tables for Attention Residuals (AttnRes).
  • Practical implication: Provides a drop-in architectural upgrade over standard residual connections for transformer models.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Kimi's Scaling Strategy Framework

  • How it works: Scales model capabilities across three orthogonal dimensions: Token Efficiency (MuonClip), Long Context (Kimi Linear Attention), and Agent Swarms.
  • Components:
    • Token Efficiency (MuonClip Optimizer)
    • Long Context (Kimi Delta Attention)
    • Agent Swarms (Orchestrator and Sub-agents)
  • When to use: When building and scaling frontier open-source foundation models.

Agent Swarms RL Reward Function

  • How it works: Guides multi-agent training using three weighted reward components to encourage effective task decomposition and completion.
  • Components:
    • Instantiation Reward (incentivizes sub-agent creation, prevents serial collapse)
    • Finish Reward (encourages completion of assigned subtasks)
    • Outcome Reward (measures whether the overall task achieves the end goal)
  • When to use: When training collaborative multi-agent systems via reinforcement learning.

## Overview
- **Speaker**: Zhilin Yang
- **Channel**: Kimi AI
- **Main topic**: Scaling strategies for open-source AI models, focusing on Kimi K2.5, MuonClip optimizer, Kimi Linear attention, attention residuals, and agent swarms.
- **Purpose**: To explain the architectural innovations and scaling laws employed by Moonshot AI in developing Kimi K2.5 and its associated open-source techniques.
Zhilin Yang, Founder and CEO of Kimi (Moonshot AI), presents the scaling strategies behind Kimi K2.5 at NVIDIA GTC 2026. The talk covers three key scaling dimensions: token efficiency via MuonClip optimizer, long context via Kimi Linear attention, and agent swarms via multi-agent reinforcement learning. Additionally, it highlights Kimi K2.5 as the first open model with native joint vision-text pretraining, achieving superior performance across modalities.
## Topic Map
### Introduction to Kimi's Scaling Strategy
- **Explanation**: Introduction of open models, democratizing intelligence, and the three primary scaling dimensions: token efficiency, long context, and agent swarms.
- **Key claims**:
  - Open models are closing the gap with proprietary models.
  - Scaling is the primary driver of major AI developments.
  - Scaling must happen across multiple dimensions: token efficiency, context length, and agent swarms.
- **Examples**:
  - Deploying open models on local servers or the cloud with full weight access.
- **Terminology**:
  - open models
  - scaling law
  - token efficiency
  - long context
  - agent swarms
- **Why it matters**: Establishes the foundational philosophy of making frontier intelligence accessible to developers worldwide.
### Token Efficiency: MuonClip Optimizer
- **Explanation**: Discusses scaling token efficiency using the Muon optimizer combined with weight decay and QK-Clip to achieve ~2x token efficiency over AdamW without training divergence.
- **Key claims**:
  - Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW.
  - Training instability during large-scale Muon training can be resolved using QK-Clip.
  - Token efficiency improves the upper bound of model intelligence, acting like a data multiplier.
- **Examples**:
  - Scaling a 1-trillion parameter model with Muon and encountering max logit explosions solved by QK-Clip.
- **Terminology**:
  - Muon optimizer
  - MuonClip
  - weight decay
  - RMS updates
  - QK-Clip
  - max logits
- **Why it matters**: Overcomes data wall limitations by maximizing intelligence per training token.
### Long Context: Kimi Linear Attention (KDA)
- **Explanation**: Introduces Kimi Linear Attention (KDA) and Kimi Linear Architecture, combining Delta Attention with a 3:1 ratio of linear to full attention layers to achieve linear scaling and superior long-context performance.
- **Key claims**:
  - Transformers outperform LSTMs asymptotically due to long-context utilization across the whole context.
  - Kimi Delta Attention improves recurrent memory management and hardware efficiency.
  - Kimi Linear architecture achieves better performance than full attention baselines while cutting memory overhead.
- **Examples**:
  - Comparing transformer and LSTM token-index scaling curves and benchmarking Kimi Linear on MMLU and RULER.
- **Terminology**:
  - Kimi Delta Attention (KDA)
  - Gated Delta Rule (GDR)
  - Kimi Linear
  - chunkwise formulation
  - matrix inversion
- **Why it matters**: Enables efficient processing of million-token context lengths without quadratic compute penalties.
### Agent Swarms and Reinforcement Learning
- **Explanation**: Explains the multi-agent swarm paradigm where an orchestrator agent delegates complex tasks to specialized sub-agents working in parallel, guided by specific reinforcement learning reward functions.
- **Key claims**:
  - Agent swarms scale task complexity beyond single-agent capabilities.
  - Reinforcement learning for agent swarms requires instantiation, finish, and outcome rewards to prevent serial collapse and spurious parallelism.
  - Agent swarms save significant execution time on complex tasks compared to single agents.
- **Examples**:
  - Writing a 100-page literature review by spawning specialized researchers and fact-checkers in parallel.
- **Terminology**:
  - agent swarms
  - orchestrator
  - sub-agents
  - instantiation reward
  - finish reward
  - outcome reward
- **Why it matters**: Solves complex, multi-step workflows by orchestrating collaborative intelligence.
### Vision-Text Joint Pretraining & Attention Residuals
- **Explanation**: Presents Kimi K2.5 as the first open model with native joint vision-text pretraining (early fusion) and introduces Attention Residuals (AttnRes) as a rotation of LSTM residuals into attention space.
- **Key claims**:
  - Early fusion vision-text joint pretraining yields better results than late fusion.
  - Vision reinforcement learning improves textual performance (cross-modal transfer).
  - Attention Residuals improve token efficiency by 24% and reduce training loss.
- **Examples**:
  - Training Kimi K2.5 on NVIDIA H800 clusters and demonstrating code, vision, and text capabilities.
- **Terminology**:
  - early fusion
  - vision-text joint pretraining
  - Attention Residuals (AttnRes)
  - block attention residual
- **Why it matters**: Unifies vision and text natively while introducing breakthrough architectural components.
## Key Points
### MuonClip doubles token efficiency over AdamW
- **Explanation**: By applying the second-order Muon optimizer with weight decay and consistent RMS updates, model training achieves equivalent intelligence with half the tokens.
- **Evidence**: Scaling law graphs showing ~2x token efficiency vs AdamW.
- **Practical implication**: Reduces training compute requirements and effectively expands limited high-quality data budgets.
### QK-Clip stabilizes large-scale Muon training
- **Explanation**: Scaling Muon to 1-trillion parameter models causes max logits to explode; QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to prevent divergence.
- **Evidence**: Validation loss and max logits training curves before and after QK-Clip.
- **Practical implication**: Allows stable training of large transformer models with advanced second-order optimizers.
### Kimi Linear Attention balances efficiency and expressivity
- **Explanation**: Using a 3:1 ratio of linear attention (Kimi Delta Attention) to full attention layers with chunkwise formulation cuts memory overhead while outperforming full attention.
- **Evidence**: Performance benchmarks on RULER and MMLU across 128k to 1M token lengths.
- **Practical implication**: Drastically reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) at long context lengths.
### Agent swarms accelerate complex task execution
- **Explanation**: Orchestrator-driven agent swarms decompose complex tasks into parallel subtasks, using specialized RL reward functions to ensure successful task completion.
- **Evidence**: Execution time vs task complexity graphs showing up to 4.5x speedups.
- **Practical implication**: Enables automated execution of complex workflows like software engineering and comprehensive research.
### Attention Residuals generalize residual connections
- **Explanation**: Treating attention as an LSTM residual rotated by 90 degrees and applying attention residuals across layers improves pretraining token efficiency by 24%.
- **Evidence**: Scaling law and benchmark comparison tables for Attention Residuals (AttnRes).
- **Practical implication**: Provides a drop-in architectural upgrade over standard residual connections for transformer models.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Kimi's Scaling Strategy Framework
- **How it works**: Scales model capabilities across three orthogonal dimensions: Token Efficiency (MuonClip), Long Context (Kimi Linear Attention), and Agent Swarms.
- **Components**:
  - Token Efficiency (MuonClip Optimizer)
  - Long Context (Kimi Delta Attention)
  - Agent Swarms (Orchestrator and Sub-agents)
- **When to use**: When building and scaling frontier open-source foundation models.
### Agent Swarms RL Reward Function
- **How it works**: Guides multi-agent training using three weighted reward components to encourage effective task decomposition and completion.
- **Components**:
  - Instantiation Reward (incentivizes sub-agent creation, prevents serial collapse)
  - Finish Reward (encourages completion of assigned subtasks)
  - Outcome Reward (measures whether the overall task achieves the end goal)
- **When to use**: When training collaborative multi-agent systems via reinforcement learning.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Training a 1-trillion parameter model with Muon optimizer without QK-Clip.
- **Illustrates**: Training instability and max logits explosion leading to divergence.
- **Lesson**: Advanced second-order optimizers require stability mechanisms like QK-Clip for large-scale training.
### Executing a 100+ word systematic literature review using K2.5 Agent Swarm.

- **Lesson**: Agent swarms dramatically reduce execution time for complex, multi-source research tasks.

- Attention Residuals improve pretraining token efficiency by 24%. (architectural)
## Notable Quotes
